discovery: Time reversal and wavefront shaping of waves in complex scattering media

nominees.name: Mathias Fink
nominees.affiliation: Institut Langevin, ESPCI Paris - PSL, France

subfield: Wave physics / optics of complex media
motivation: Multiple scattering was long seen as the end of coherent wave control. Mathias Fink showed with time-reversal mirrors that disorder can be used: a wave sent back in time through a complex medium refocuses on its source, and it focuses more sharply because of the scattering. This established a general principle across acoustics, electromagnetism and seismology. In 2007 Ivo Vellekoop and Allard Mosk carried the idea into optics. By shaping the incident wavefront, they focused light through an opaque layer with an enhancement of about a thousand. They also showed that mesoscopic correlations, including open channels, give practical control over transmission. Together these works founded the field of wavefront shaping. Its outgrowths include transmission-matrix measurement, imaging through and inside biological tissue, deep-brain endoscopy through multimode fibres, physical optical computing and high-dimensional quantum photonics. This is fundamental wave physics that turned a basic limitation into a widely used tool.
